nfl.vote_outcome_model.mechanism: Winner or rank probability from candidate quality, narrative, previous votes, timing and electorate composition, aggregated through each award's actual ballot, which is a PARAMETER of the model per award and season: voters V, places K and points vector w. AP ballot parameters per award and season, each with its evidence status. (a) MVP, 2025 season: 50 voters, 5 places, points 10-5-3-2-1; seen in search-result copies of AP wire text, AP primary page not fetched. (b) MVP, 2023 season: 5 places, points 10-5-3-2-1 (a per-position tally such as 49-0-1-0-0=493 was seen in a search copy); primary not fetched. (c) The other seven AP awards, 2025 season: 5 places, points 10-5-3-2-1, 50-voter panel; seen in search-result copies of the AP finalist and results text, primary not fetched. (d) MVP from 2022 as a top-5 ballot with only the top three places for the other awards (5-3-1): reported in search copies of an AP statement, UNVERIFIED, and the season in which the non-MVP awards moved to five places is unknown. (e) Single first-place vote before 2022: UNVERIFIED. (f) Voter count for seasons other than 2025, the tie rule and the ballot close date: not found. (g) The tally Stafford 366 points / 24 firsts versus Maye 361 / 23 is reported in search copies as the 2025-season MVP result; the page date of one cited URL was ambiguous, so the season attribution is unconfirmed.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.measurement: Per AP award, model each voter's ranked ballot: rank-ordered (exploded) logit of candidate placements on features (team win% at ballot close, statistical rank within position by EPA or season totals, prior award wins, position dummy), ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, prior weight 3 pseudo-observations; fit seasons whose full AP placement counts are published, with K, V and w read per award and season from the ballot-parameter table in the mechanism (not hard-coded) and any single-vote seasons on first-place votes only as a separate regime sharing feature weights through a hierarchical prior. Simulate V ballots per draw (V=50 is seen in search copies for 2025 only) and score each with the points vector w of that award-season (10-5-3-2-1 seen in search copies for the MVP and, in 2025, the other AP awards; any other scheme is read from that season's AP tally), winner = highest points (ties shared). Non-AP processes (PFWA Executive of the Year, Hall of Fame, All-Pro, T100) keep their own model: T100 ordered logit on previous rank, change in production, position group, age. Output P(candidate=winner) and P(rank=r); group markets P(group) = sum of P(win) by team at announcement time with 1/N co-winner payout; Executive of the Year tie probability = own-award co-winner frequency shrunk to comparable awards with weight 10. As-of ballot close.

nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.rationale: AP awards are ranked-points ballots (MVP 10-5-3-2-1 over five places and, in 2025, the other AP awards too, all seen in search-result copies with the AP primary page not fetched; earlier non-MVP schemes are reported but unverified), so two similar candidates split first places but not all support: a candidate can win on second- and third-place points (reported in search copies as the 2025 MVP tally: Stafford 366 points with 24 firsts, Maye 361 with 23; season attribution unconfirmed). A penalty fitted to first-place shares under plurality overstates the split for ranked seasons and must be estimated by regime.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.measurement: Rank-ordered logit latent utility for candidate i on voter ballot = x_i'theta - beta_r x max over same-team or same-position rivals j of x_j'theta, where x are the nfl.vote_outcome_model features and r indexes the placement (first place versus lower places). Estimate theta and beta_r by maximum likelihood on placement counts per candidate for seasons with published AP placement counts, with places K and points w read per award and season (see the ballot-parameter table in nfl.vote_outcome_model; evidence status per parameter is explicit there), and on first-place vote shares under a Dirichlet-multinomial for the pre-2022 seasons as a separate single-vote regime (the single-vote format is UNVERIFIED and the 2005 start is an arbitrary sample window); ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, shrink beta_r toward 0. Output winner probabilities from simulated V-voter ballots scored by that award-season's points vector. As-of ballot close.

nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.rationale: Both contracts are low-rate Bernoulli events whose base rate differs strongly by coach and personnel (for example a former-quarterback receiver, or a team that favours quarterback sneaks at the 1; both are hypotheses to test, not measured facts); league averages mislead, but team samples are tiny, so heavy shrinkage toward the league rate is essential and stakes may raise trick-play frequency.
nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.measurement: Non-QB pass: count of pass attempts by players whose roster position is not QB per team-game over the last 3 seasons, shrunk to league rate (about 0.15 per game, to recompute) with k=40 team-games, coach random effect; P(any in game) = 1 - exp(-(rate_A + rate_B)). Pass from the 1: expected snaps with yardline_100 <= 1 per team-game (from drives reaching the 1, last 2 seasons, shrink k=30) x team pass share on those snaps (shrink to league about 0.35 with k=25 snaps) counting official forward pass attempts only; sacks, scrambles and runs must be excluded explicitly (whether the nflverse pass_attempt flag already excludes sacks, how no_play rows are treated and how spikes are flagged are UNVERIFIED); P(at least one) by Poisson. As-of kickoff with the active roster.

nfl.script.mechanism: Teams pass more and play faster when trailing and run and slow down when leading; the expected game script from the own-model expected margin (not the betting spread) therefore determines volume splits between passing and rushing props.
nfl.script.measurement: From play_by_play estimate pass rate, seconds/play, rush attempts and efficiency as a function of score differential bins and time remaining; simulate or integrate with the distribution of game states implied by the market-free margin and total distributions of nfl.model_team_points_mean and nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd (e.g., a Gaussian or t margin around the own-model mean margin); betting spreads and totals are not used; team-specific slope with shrinkage to league.

nfl.weekly_slate_composition.mechanism: Which teams and games are in the week's slate: byes remove teams, Week 18 includes all 32, and international or Thursday games are part of the same week; the game count N of the slate is the exposure of weekly count and maximum contracts.
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.rationale: The slate size N (about 13 to 16 games and 26 to 32 teams per week) is the exposure of weekly count and weekly maximum contracts, and a team on bye contributes no game, which a market text may not say explicitly.

nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.measurement: Do not build a separate simulator: use the single shared season simulator nfl.standings_sim (with the shared rating-uncertainty draw and tie probability of the win-totals record, 0.25 percent per game and rating prior sd of 4.0 points as the shared assumptions) run on REMAINING games only, conditioned on the results already played as of the current week (completed scores, ties, each team's current win streak and undefeated flag, banked ties), current injuries and quarterback status. For each of 100,000 runs record: the longest streak (under both tie treatments, see u2) for each team, the week of each team's first loss (ties not losses; same-week first losses tied), season tie count (banked + simulated), and the worst-to-first indicator; output probabilities for each contract rung.

nfl.two_minute_tempo.measurement: Per team: points, plays and pass rate in the last two minutes of each half, share of end-of-half possessions with points; opponent-adjusted; timeouts retained; QB prior in two-minute drill; combine with lead/trail states from the own-model margin distribution (nfl.model_team_points_mean and nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd), not from betting spreads or totals.

nfl.ot_model.mechanism: Overtime frequency, the overtime rule set in force that season and tie probability determine settlement of regulation-only versus including-OT markets. (Rule history as stated in the original draft and NOT verified from a primary rulebook in this round; treat as unverified secondary information.) From 2025 the regular-season overtime is a single 10-minute period in which both teams get a possession (an opening-drive touchdown no longer ends the game), then sudden death; the game is a tie if the period expires level. Seasons 2017-2024 used the 10-minute first-possession-touchdown-wins format; the playoffs have no time limit.
nfl.ot_model.rationale: OT adds scoring and changes winner markets; in nflverse regular-season data (2012-2025, n=3,784, figures from the original draft and not re-checked here) about 6% of games were tied after regulation and went to overtime, but only about 0.4% ended tied, so markets that settle on regulation carry meaningful tie mass while including-OT markets almost none; ties count 0.5 in standings. The overtime rule set changes by season and must be read from each contract's rules text, not assumed. Market wording must be matched to the model.

nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era.mechanism: Rule changes may alter ball flight and attempt opportunities: a 2025 rule letting kickers prepare kicking balls is reported (secondary news only; primary rulebook not fetched; UNVERIFIED) to have been followed by a jump in 60+ yard makes, and the fair-catch free kick is described as allowing an unrushed attempt scored as a field goal (UNVERIFIED).

nfl.fg_attempt_hazard_by_distance_band_6.measurement: From play-by-play over the last 4 seasons count attempts with official kick length in each band per team-game and qualifying situations (game_seconds_remaining in half <= 20, offence with yardline_100 between 43 and 62 so that the kick length, about yardline_100 + 17 yards, is 60 to 79 yards (a 60-yard kick is snapped from about the opponent 43), score differential in {-3..0} at half end, plus venue altitude and roof); estimate P(attempt in band | situation) by a hierarchical logit with head coach and kicker random effects (kicker max made kick, 60+ history, wind, rule era including the K-ball regime of nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era), shrinking coach rates to the league with 15 qualifying situations of prior weight. Output expected attempts per band for each remaining team-game and the league total for the remaining schedule; make probability by band comes from nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model and nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail. As-of kickoff with the active kicker.

nfl.team_window_game_exposure.measurement: From the official schedule as of the market's issuance timestamp T, for team t build the rung ladder of windows: for each end week W in {2,4,6,8,12,14,16} and 'anytime' (the whole regular season) the window of rung W is the set of regular-season games with week < W (these rungs were reported by a reviewer from Kalshi API metadata, not by the sampled rules text, and are unverified); compute N_g(W) for every rung (from 1 to about 17 games) so nested windows share the same game list. For each game record week, kickoff time, opponent, home or road, roof and bye weeks (a bye contributes no game). Game g is inside a window if kickoff_g > T; a game in progress at T is flagged IN_PROGRESS and carried with both readings (counted with remaining plays only versus excluded) because the sampled text does not say; the reviewer reports the nine sampled markets were all opened before Week 1 (unverified), in which case no game is in progress at issuance. Attach to each game the as-of distribution over the opponent's starting quarterback from nfl.qb and nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model (widening with weeks ahead, up to 17 weeks for the longest rung). Recompute whenever the schedule changes (flex, postponement, relocation) and flag postponed games and their new week. Output the game table with features and the N_g(W) ladder.

nfl.window_hazard_survival_with_game_cor.mechanism: Turns per-game event hazards into the probability of at least one event over each nested window of a rung ladder as one minus the expected product of per-game zero-event probabilities, averaging over shared uncertainty (the team's defensive quality, scheme changes, quarterback injuries) that links the games.
nfl.window_hazard_survival_with_game_cor.measurement: Per game g for team t: expected event count lambda_g = D_g x p0 x m_def(t) x m_qb(q_g), where D_g = expected opposing dropbacks (opposing plays from nfl.pace and nfl.total_plays_state_model times the opposing dropback rate; nfl.proe is a pass-rate-over-expected input whose pass-attempt versus dropback definition is not verified, so the dropback rate must be re-measured as qb_dropback per play, sacks and scrambles included, and p0 is defined per qb_dropback to match), p0 = league interceptions per dropback, m_def(t) = the named team's defensive interception multiplier relative to the league (a ratio, not a rate): a base multiplier from nfl.opp_def_int_propensity (already adjusted for the quality of quarterbacks faced) times an availability-and-scheme adjustment A(t) as of T, where A(t) is estimated by regressing past team interception multipliers on the snap-weighted availability of cornerbacks and safeties from nfl.def_personnel (injury and absence vintages) and on the change in man/zone and single-high/two-high shell rates from nfl.coverage_scheme versus the base period (these inputs measure availability and scheme, not ball skills, so ball-skill differences enter only through the team's own past takeaways), and m_qb(q_g) = the opposing quarterback's multiplier relative to the league (a ratio) from nfl.int_rate, estimated net of the defences he has faced; the two multipliers are ratios so that no per-attempt rate is multiplied by another and the quarterback is not counted twice (if m_def were not quarterback-adjusted it must not be combined with m_qb). The team's takeaway rate uses the interception flag only (fumble recoveries excluded); nfl.turnovers is a regression benchmark, not the rate. Draw a shared log-multiplier u_t ~ Normal(0, tau^2) for the defence (tau to be fitted from between-season variation of team interception rates after shrinkage) and draw each game's opposing starter from its as-of distribution. Survival to the end of rung W: S(W) = E[ product over games with week < W of exp(-lambda_g exp(u_t)) ]; compute every rung from the same draws so S(W) is non-increasing in W and P(at least one by W) = 1 - S(W) is monotone across the nested rungs. Report with and without the shared factor. As-of issuance timestamp and recomputed after each game.
raw_data: per-team-game defensive interceptions (interception flag) and opposing dropbacks
per-quarterback interception rates relative to league
schedule window table and rung ladder from nfl.team_window_game_exposure
opposing plays and dropback rates from pace and PROE inputs
defensive-back participation and injury vintages by team-week; coverage-shell rates by team-season

nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.mechanism: Negative-binomial dispersion parameters and mean multipliers for the in-game counts settled by this archetype (field goals, sacks, total yards and successful two-point and fourth-down conversions) by score state and game total; interceptions and rush attempts are not settled by any series here and are out of scope.
raw_data: team-game counts: FG made, sacks, total yards, successful 2-point and 4th-down conversions
nfl.count_stat_dispersion_and_state_spli.measurement: From 2012-2025 team-games fit, per stat (field goals, sacks, total yards, conversions), a negative binomial with mean = opportunities x rate and dispersion k by stat and by score-state bucket (lead>=14, within 7, trail>=14); shrink k toward the league-stat value with a gamma prior (equivalent to 200 team-games); output PMF for each stat given expected mean and state mixture over the pre-game margin distribution.

nfl.leader_order_statistic.mechanism: Leader markets resolve to the maximum across many players with correlated outcomes; the probability that a given player leads depends on the top-end distribution of competitors, not just his own mean. Use by archetype: in statistical-leader markets this is the winner rule (Monte Carlo P(max)); in vote-based award markets (season_awards) it is only a production-rank feature that feeds ballot placement in nfl.vote_outcome_model and is not the winner rule.
nfl.leader_order_statistic.measurement: Simulate distributions for each contender (using player_stat_variance and games_played_dist) and compute P(max) by Monte Carlo; for weekly leaders include all players on the slate; calibrate against historical leader frequencies. For vote-based awards, output only each candidate's simulated production rank among peers as a feature of the ballot model; the winner there is decided by simulated ranked-ballot points.

nfl.qb.measurement: Probability distribution over starting QB from practice participation (DNP/limited/full), team designation, coach statements and history of QBs with similar injuries; QB value in points (starter minus replacement) estimated from own-model team ratings with and without the quarterback (nfl.own_team_rating_market_free), not from betting line moves; map to team ratings under each scenario and mix by probability; timestamp each information vintage.
free_sources: nflverse injuries (weekly practice and game status)
NFL official injury reports (nfl.com; Wed-Fri practice reports, game-day inactives about 90 min pre-kick)
ESPN public JSON (site.api.espn.com scoreboard / summary / injuries; odds fields not used)
nflverse games.csv (roof, surface, temp, wind, rest, referee, coaches, starting QBs; betting columns dropped)

nfl.award_stats.measurement: Candidate features: EPA, yards, TDs, team wins, rank among peers; historical winner models using logistic regression on past awards (QB bias, team record threshold); track media poll mentions (not betting or prediction-market odds); update weekly.
